questions.stem: The point (3, 5) is reflected in the line y = 2. What are the coordinates of the image?
questions.explanation: The point (3, 5) is 3 units above y = 2, so its image is 3 units below: y = 2 − 3 = −1. The x-coordinate stays the same. A common error is reflecting in y = 0 (the x-axis), which gives (3, −5).

questions.stem: A triangle has a vertex at (−4, 1). After reflection, the image of this vertex is at (1, −4). What is the line of reflection?
questions.explanation: Under reflection in y = x, the point (a, b) maps to (b, a). Here (−4, 1) maps to (1, −4), which swaps the coordinates. This confirms the mirror line is y = x.

questions.stem: Point A(2, 7) is reflected in the line x = 5. What are the coordinates of A'?
questions.explanation: The point (2, 7) is 3 units to the left of x = 5, so its image is 3 units to the right: x = 5 + 3 = 8. The y-coordinate is unchanged, giving (8, 7). Option (b) is a common error from miscounting the distance.

questions.stem: A shape is reflected in the y-axis and then reflected in the x-axis. Point P(3, −2) on the original shape ends up at which point?
questions.explanation: Reflecting (3, −2) in the y-axis gives (−3, −2). Then reflecting in the x-axis gives (−3, 2). This combined transformation is equivalent to a 180° rotation about the origin.

questions.stem: The point (1, 6) is reflected in the line y = −x. What are the coordinates of the image?
questions.explanation: Under reflection in y = −x, the point (a, b) maps to (−b, −a). So (1, 6) maps to (−6, −1). A common mistake is using the y = x rule (swapping without negating), which gives (6, 1).
